title: Proof ok
statement: Prove that for every integer $n$ the number $n^5 + 5n^3 - 6n$ is divisible by $6$.
hints: Divisibility by $6$ splits into two conditions.
solution: Write $n^5 + 5n^3 - 6n = n(n^2 - 1)(n^2 + 6) $, which holds because $(n^2-1)(n^2+6) = n^4 + 5n^2 - 6$. The product $(n-1)n(n+1)$ of three consecutive integers is divisible by both $2$ and $3$, hence by $6$, and it divides the expression. So the expression is divisible by $6$.

rubric.criterion: Factorises the expression or reduces to residues.
